abstract: Extracting useful network management information from a large volume of QoS data obtained all over a network can be simplified by innovative data mining techniques. The need for QoS expertise is reduced as interactive visualization by brushing and linking of datasets reveals interrelation of parameters. Data contextualization by annotated data can aid the assessment on the global level of compatibility between supply and use conditions. Data dashboards can further simplify the analysis of QoS data by recognizing the network connectivity of different sites, seasonal effects and direction of voltage waveform events.

articleTitle: Analysis of tuned filters for mitigation of harmonic current distortion of air conditioning systems to inverter
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to analyze the harmonic current distortion in a system with air conditioners driven by frequency converters and its correction waveform current with the use of two filters tuned in different frequencies. The use of air conditioners inverter, despite lower power consumption, the circuit injects harmonic frequencies of multiple orders that pollute the system. The filters used here are tuned to harmonics of 5th and 3rd order. Thus the filters are installed with the aim of minimizing these distortions and improve the quality of electric power system. In this context, through computer simulations, was observed the effectiveness of both passive filters tuned aiming to reduce the levels of harmonic distortion in the current on bus.

articleTitle: AC-machine with frequency converter with immunity to voltage dips
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper solves problematic of supply voltage dips and their influence to modern electric drive (i.e. induction machine supplied from indirect frequency converter). The paper presents the control algorithms for basic variant the most used drives (with non-controlled rectifier and without additional converter) and variants with more complicated power circuits (with active rectifier respectively with special additional step-up boost converter in DC-link).

articleTitle: Unified power flow controller performance
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper aims to present a comparative analysis of a computationally implemented model of an Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) and an ASC (Advanced Series Compensator) through case studies. To do so, a description its principle of operation and mathematical modeling, comprehending the series and parallel compensators, is given so that the control objectives can be determined using the vector theory.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis and modeling of the electromagnetic interferences in integrated planar structures
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper outlines a method for the suppression of the parasitic inside electromagnetic interferences (EMI) filters that are used in power supply devices. The paper focuses on EMI filters designed using the electromagnetic integrated planar technology. To accomplish this task the authors set up an optimal design algorithm named OptimCond that is able to find out the optimal arrangement of the windings in order to minimize the structural parasitic capacitance of the filter. The algorithm proposed is applied to increase the EMI filtering performances for a well-known filter realized in planar technology.

articleTitle: An alternative strategy for emulating mechanical loads on the shaft of induction machines subject to power quality disturbances
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: For a laboratory evaluation of the effects of PQ phenomena on three-phase induction motors (TIM), one of the challenges is to set up equipment that allows adjusting the machine's nominal current and selecting the type of load to be driven. Direct Current Generators (DCG) can be used to emulate different kinds of mechanical loads on the motor shaft. To do this, it is necessary to adopt a control strategy which allows variation of the load torque according to the profile desired. In this paper, the proposed strategy is compared with one conventionally adopted and it is applied to a study of a TIM's performance. This type of research makes it possible to investigate the effects of PQ disturbances on a TIM.

articleTitle: Behavioral and statistical analysis of total harmonic distortion input frequency converter of a triggering an industrial fan: A case study
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: In the context of power quality the harmonics problems are regulated by normative recommendation based on levels of individual and total distortions by ANEEL - Brazil (National Electric Energy Agency). This paper outlines and implements methodology for mathematical and statistical analysis of the behavior of the total harmonic distortion of voltage and current at the input of a frequency converter feeding an induction motor common, coupled to a mechanical centrifugal fan. The results show a trend of decreasing harmonic distortion with increasing frequency drive the load in question.

articleTitle: An over-voltage protection scheme of power capacitor bank exposed to harmonic
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper analyzed the defects of the most conventional protections of the capacitor when voltage waveform distortion is serious, and the effects on the protections of voltage signal selection in harmonic case. These defects may cause tripping failure or mal operation of protection in serious harmonic condition. Then this paper researched the influence of harmonics on capacitor life by an experiment and analyzed the relationship between the change of capacity value and voltage rms (root mean square), peak and waveform factor before and after the test. According to the capacitor over-voltage protection defects and combined with capacitor test results, this paper proposed an over-voltage protection scheme based on voltage peak and waveform factor. This scheme retains the original rms over-voltage protection, adds protection strategy aimed at voltage peak and waveform factor and a concrete proposal is given to realize the specific protection. By this method, capacitor bank could be protected effectively.

articleTitle: Lightning study of windfarm collector system
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical modeling and simulation of a lightning study of 115kV and 34.5kV overhead line (OH) connected to windfarm collector system. The electromagnetic transient program PSCAD/EMTDC is used to model and simulate the OH line and other substation equipment. Shielding failure and back flashover studies are performed to characterize the magnitude of the lightning overvoltages. The effect of variation in tower grounding resistance on lightning overvoltages is also analysed. Insulation requirements and protective ratios of main transformers, wind turbine generator (WTG) transformer and circuit breakers are verified with respect to voltage developed during lightning. The protective ratios are compared as per IEEE std C62.22-1997.

articleTitle: Power quality deterioration due complex behavior of a power inverter with a three-phase-rotary induction motor load
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper shows the behavior of a three-phase power converter with Rotary Induction Motor (RIM) load using quasi-sliding and chaos control techniques for output voltage regulation. Controller is designed using Zero Average Dynamic (ZAD) and Fixed Point Inducting Control (FPIC) techniques. Designs have been tested in a Rapid Control Prototyping (RCP) system based on Digital Signal Processing (DSP) on dSPACE platform. Bifurcation diagrams show the robustness of the system. Chaos detection is a signal processing method in the time domain, and has power quality phenomena detection applications. Results show that the phase voltage in the load has sinusoidal performance when it is controlled with these techniques.

articleTitle: Power quality disturbances segmentation based on wavelet decomposition and adaptive thresholds
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper proposes an automatic method for determining an adaptive threshold based on Wavelet decomposition, which allows the segmentation of power quality signals. Primarily, these signals were synthetically generated, which represents short duration voltage variations, oscillatory and impulsive transients and harmonic distortions. Subsequently, the signals were decomposed by Daubechies Wavelets, whose second level of decomposition provided the values of energy and entropy of the energy used in determining the adaptive thresholds. The segments were then obtained by the intersections of the curves of Wavelets details with the calculated thresholds. The results reached with this methodology were evaluated under synthetic and real oscillographs in order to show its efficiency.

articleTitle: Identification of relative component participation in harmonic measurements
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: When harmonic resonance problems exist in large networks, it can be difficult to identify the extent to which various capacitors and inductors in the system contribute to these problems. This paper attempts to address this issue by presenting a new method for identifying the relative participation of capacitors and inductors on the amplification of harmonics in the system. Specifically the participation of system capacitors and inductors to a particular voltage (or current) harmonic will be identified. This proposed method combines concepts of steady state analysis and modal analysis to identify dimensionless indices that quantify the participation of each capacitor and inductor to particular harmonic measurements. This method is validated through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Concept of stochastic measurements in the Fourier domain
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of measurement of a crucial quantities in the public distribution network using the Fourier coefficients. The method for Fourier coefficients measurement is presented, as well as the instrument by which the measurement is performed. The accuracy of the measured coefficients is between 14 and 15 bits of FS.

articleTitle: The influence of reactive flow by electronic loads in electricity billing system
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper analyzes the use of a set of electronic loads, specifically tubular and compact fluorescent lamps with electronic ballasts to offset the reactive excess of an inductive load, as well as its possible impact on existing rules of charging. In laboratory measurements using CFLs was observed a capacitive reactive power flow to the source. When added in parallel to a bank of inductors, the power factor was offset by reactive lamps. In measurements made in the field on a bus comprising tubular fluorescent lamps with electronic ballasts, also was found capacitive reactive flow toward the source. Using the software ATP Draw was modeled a set of compact fluorescent lamps which confirmed the results found in the laboratory. In this work was analyzed whether this capacitive reactive flow generated by electronic loads can be beneficial or detrimental to the charging system, depending on the time of day that the electronic charge is triggered.

articleTitle: Another case of discrepancies when evaluating power theories using real data
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Most non-sinusoidal power theories have been developed from theoretical techniques, as well as relying on hypothetical and experimental networks to highlight the advantages of each. The drawback of the power theories is that no single one has been universally accepted as a benchmark for other developments. This paper will however show this weakness by means of evaluating two power theories in the time domain, using real recorded data.

articleTitle: Design of special DC-source with minimizing of its negative impact to the supply network
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper describes the problems of design of special high power DC current source 110V/1kA. Focus was placed on the issue of minimizing the negative impact of this power source on low-frequency disturbance in power supply network.

articleTitle: Global sensitivity and uncertainty analysis of Transients in the Universal Line Model
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: One of the main aspects of designing and operation prediction of any power system is to simulate its Electromagnetic Transient's (EMT) performance. Among the available power line models, Universal Line Model (ULM) is an efficient and accurate model for this purpose. There are random system parameters which affect the quantities of EMT output qualities. This paper presents a novel global sensitivity and uncertainty analysis techniques to determine the effect of these uncertain factors on the variation of the EMT outputs.

articleTitle: Equivalent electrical diagram of a simple longitudinal unbalance in an electric network in three-phase sinusoidal regime
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This work aims at resolving the issue of a model that uses symmetrical mathematical components, dedicated to longitudinal simple unbalance for three phase radial transmission electrical lines of an electricity distribution system. The symmetrical component of both current and voltage are obtained, as well as values of the electric distribution system parameters, in order to determine imbalance factors which may characterize quality of supply service for the electricity end-users.

articleTitle: An analysis of power quality of Matrix Converters when using a Fryze reference
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Static power converters produce harmonics due to the nature of the conversion process. This paper will investigate the effect on the power factor of a sinusoidal and Fryze current reference on Matrix Converters. It has been shown in previous papers that a Fryze current ref is best. This paper will develop a mathematical model, based on the single sided Fourier expansion. Using this mathematical model it will be shown that even though a high harmonic content could be present in a Fryze controlled Matrix Converter; the power factor will have been improved.

articleTitle: Power quality assessment by entropy
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper presents another way to assess power quality delivered by transformers. It has been shown that is possible to measure the wave form irregularity of electrical signals radiated by electrical systems by means of the sample entropy algorithm. The electro-magnetic signal entropy reveals the presence of harmonics in the industrial and domestic electric power supply. It will show magnetic radiated wave measurements taken in the closest point to the transformer PCC, through a non-invasive and indirect measurement (using wireless magnetic sensor).

articleTitle: Solutions to optimize energy consumption of airblowers by monitoring oxygen levels in the bioreactor
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The paper deals with the analysis of energy consumption and power quality in wastewater treatment plants, during the operation of air blowers optimized for monitoring the level of oxygen in the bioreactor. The airblowers' consumption is over 68% in energy consumption of wastewater treatment plant. This consumption optimization was done using sensors of the level of oxygen in the bioreactor that partial closure for command of airblowers, maintaining oxygen levels between 1.5 and 2.5%. By closing the discharge of airblowers it reduce the air flow, the rotation frequency of airblower and its consumption. The current absorbed during the operation of these airblowers shows important harmonics.

articleTitle: Auto-cross correlation coefficients used for detecting an internal fault in three phase transformer
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A new algorithm based on correlation coefficients analysis of waveforms to detect an internal fault occurs in three phase transformer is proposed. The algorithm depends on the changes in current waveform that occur during internal fault. Auto-correlation has been added to cross-correlation algorithm for enhancing the security and speed in detecting the fault within very short time. It is able to detect the fault after just 0.4 msec from incidence of fault occurrence. The scheme has been tested by using Matlab/Simulink software [1]. The test results show that the internal fault even inter-turn type can be correctly identified from external fault. The algorithm is simple and can be experimentally implemented.

articleTitle: The superposition of the random harmonic phasors based on the cloud model
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: A novel method based on the cloud model for the superposition of the distributed random power harmonics is presented in this paper. Three characteristic quantities (E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>, E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>) of the measured harmonic phasors are calculated by the cloud model inverse generator. The probability density function described by the cloud model is presented to obtain the 95% probability value of the harmonics. Field tests results prove that the presented method has a good performance even with small volume of samples, which does not need the particular probability distribution of each random phasor.

articleTitle: Power flow estimation based on power transformer plate data and voltage measurement
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper proposes a algorithm capable of estimating the current and power flowing through the power transformer based on the plate data and the power transformer phase voltages. The proposal must be applied on power quality monitors when only voltage records are available. The installation of power quality monitors using voltage and current measurements could not be possible without shutdown the system to install current probes and the current signals are not so available as voltage signals. Measuring only the phase voltage at both sides of a transformer and using the proposed algorithm is a suitable solution to estimate the positive, negative, and zero sequence currents and the apparent power flowing through the transformer. The currents and power flow estimated could be useful when the power quality monitor is used to locate the voltage sag source. The performance of the proposed algorithm is assessed through a real time digital simulation case study in a Brazilian utility system where the accuracy and error sensibility are evaluated.

articleTitle: Double Domain Simulation - modelling the harmonic effect of different nonlinear loads
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The concept of the Double Domain Simulation method was introduced on the 12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> ICHQP in 2006 in Cascais, Portugal. This novel method was introduced to improve the accuracy of the frequency domain simulation. To calculate the sophisticated model of a nonlinear load a time dependent model must be used. The supply network together with the high voltage upstream network could be calculated in frequency domain. An iteration algorithm was developed converting the variables in every iteration step between the time and frequency domain. This is the so called Double Domain Simulation. Between 2006 and 2014 the practical application of this novel method was introduced through several research tasks. This paper would like to give an overview about these projects, and besides this it would like to demonstrate the various application possibilities of the Double Domain Simulation method.

articleTitle: Architecture and functionalities of a smart Distribution Management System
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: The paper presents the current state of art of a developed smart Distribution Management System (DMS) environment based on the innovative SCADA systems. The tool is designed to intelligently manage, on-line and off-line, the distribution systems with a high penetration of dispersed generation and is particularly adapted to the specifics of the distribution systems in Italy. The work results from the research project InGrid done by Siemens Italy in cooperation with Politecnico di Milano and Università degli Studi di Milano universities. Research activities have been carried out for innovative functions for the management of medium voltage distribution grids in presence of distributed generation. Such functions have been deployed in a software tool and have been tested in real life conditions.

articleTitle: Multi-period power loss optimization with limited number of switching actions for enhanced continuous power supply
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: This paper deals with multi-period active power loss minimization. We formulate this problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, including constraints that specifically limit the number of switching actions between two successive anticipated system states. We solve this problem using the Mixed Integer Hybrid Differential Evolution (MIHDE), a modified Differential Evolution algorithm, which we adapt for our application. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is proven using a 60-bus system.

articleTitle: A review of recent investigations on voltage unbalance management: Further contributions to improvement of IEC/TR 61000-3-13:2008
publicationTitle: 2014 16th International Conference on Harmonics and Quality of Power (ICHQP)
abstract: Voltage unbalance (VU) management in power systems essentially involves two major aspects: VU emission allocation at the pre-connection stage and compliance assessment at the post-connection stage of installations. This is a summary and a review paper on the recent investigations completed in relation to VU emission assessment techniques which provide further contributions to the improvement of IEC Technical Report IEC/TR61000-3-13:2008. Generalised approaches developed for the classification of different sources of unbalance at the point of evaluation (covering both radial and interconnected networks) and the evaluation of their individual contributions giving emphasis to the discrimination between customer and network responsibility on VU emission are summarised. Some of the key aspects used in the IEC VU emission allocation methodology which were reviewed using rigorous outcomes of the proposed VU emission assessment techniques are presented in the paper.
